turns.question: i am an employee of a board of park commissioners, how is my pension calculated?
turns.answer:
Under Article 12, the fixed-benefit formula applies if you withdraw on or after December 31, 2003, and meet the Code’s age and service requirements: age 50 or over with at least 10 years of service, or age 60 or over with at least 4 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133(a)]

The annuity is based on 2.40% for each year of service, using your highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years before withdrawal. Service of less than a full year is prorated. If you retire before age 60, the annuity is reduced by 1/4 of 1% for each month or fraction of a month before age 60, unless you are age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service. The annuity is capped at 80% of that average annual salary. [40 ILCS 5/12-133(a)]

I’m going by your confirmation that Article 12 applies; your record currently shows Article 11. Your salary, service, averages, age at withdrawal, and retirement date on file are administered under Article 11 and are not the right basis for an Article 12 figure. The fund must correct your record first. After that, the fund would need your age at withdrawal, credited service, highest average salary for the applicable 4 consecutive years, and date of birth to determine the Article 12 amount. The earlier fixed-benefit rates apply only to withdrawals before December 31, 2003, and the accumulation-based provisions apply only to employees in service before July 1, 1971. [40 ILCS 5/12-133(a)-(b); 40 ILCS 5/12-130]

The Code does not determine the record correction; the fund owns that recordkeeping decision.

turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. For a qualifying employee, the formula is based on years of service and the highest average annual salary during a specified period before withdrawal. The section also provides different formulas that may be elected, depending on your withdrawal date, age, and service.

- For withdrawal on or after January 1, 2002, with at least 20 years of service, one election is an annuity based on 2.40% for each year of service and the highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- That elected annuity generally begins no earlier than age 55, or age 50 for an employee with at least 30 years of service, and is reduced 0.25% for each month or fractional month the annuity begins before age 60. The reduction does not apply in certain cases, including retirement at age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service or at age 55 or over with at least 25 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- The section also contains a minimum-annuity formula for an employee who withdraws at age 60 or over with at least 20 years of service. That formula uses separate rates for the first 10 years, the next 10 years, service over 20 but not over 30 years, and service over 30 years. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- An employee with at least 10 years of service who withdraws on or after January 1, 1999 may elect another formula beginning no earlier than age 60. For a withdrawal on or after January 1, 2002, it uses 2.4% for each year of service and is subject to an 80% maximum of final average salary. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your age, service, and salary figures are listed, but no annuity amount was worked out here. To calculate a dollar amount, the applicable withdrawal date and the annuity starting date are needed.

turns.question: What retirement annuity does Article 8 provide for a police officer with 25 years?
turns.answer:
Article 8 provides a retirement annuity based on the police officer’s service and highest average annual salary, with the exact rule depending on age, withdrawal date, and the applicable election under Section 8-138. [40 ILCS 5/8-138]

- With at least 20 years of service, an employee may qualify for one of several annuity formulas. Some formulas begin no earlier than age 55 and may reduce the annuity before age 60. Other formulas remove that reduction when the employee meets specified age and service conditions. [40 ILCS 5/8-138]
- The calculation generally uses the highest average annual salary for 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/8-138]
- A police officer’s service counts as city employee service for Article 8 purposes, but post-effective-date service requires the required payment to the Fund before separation, unless the statutory exception applies. [40 ILCS 5/8-227]
- Your own pension comes under Article 11, not Article 8. Article 8 also provides that a person cannot receive service credit in two city pension funds for the same period. [40 ILCS 5/8-227]

A dollar estimate would require the Article 8 member’s applicable withdrawal date, age when the annuity would begin, and highest average annual salary under the applicable formula.
